main_body: A wooden rack base box (rows 26-46) holding three upright spears; the base is drawn as a front-facing wooden crate with horizontal bands and a dark outline.
top_band: none; the base starts at row 26 with a dark outline row, then a light orange line (row 27, 1 row) and a mid-brown band, which is only a thin edge line and not a top surface. The spears above are vertical shafts.
evidence: In the column scan the base runs: dark outline row 26, a 1-row light line at row 27 (L=157), then rows 28-29 in mid brown, and the rest is front face with bands and a dark divider at 31, 36 and 46. The base has no horizontal surface visible from above. The 1-row light line is a rim, not a top. The shelf divisions and the compartments are painted flat on the front. The legs and the shafts are vertical. This is a front elevation with a thin lip, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 13 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 17-20 and 38-40 colours for the references, so it is clearly lower in density. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which fits Beodeul's approach. The wood bands have only a few steps (dark, mid, light line), and the spear shafts are flat single-tone strips with no grain. The steel tips have about 3 tones. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the stall and the well, which carry per-material texture and 5-6 shading steps.
